args.subject: Pasta recipes from Chef Mia's workshop
args.body:
Hi Alice,

I wanted to share the two traditional Italian pasta recipes I learned at Chef Mia's Culinary Studio: spaghetti alla carbonara and fettuccine Alfredo.

1) Spaghetti alla Carbonara
Ingredients (serves 4):
- 400 g spaghetti
- 150 g guanciale (or pancetta)
- 3 large eggs (or 2 whole eggs + 1 egg yolk)
- 1 cup (about 100 g) finely grated Pecorino Romano
- Freshly ground black pepper
- Salt (for the pasta water)

Method:
- Cook spaghetti in well-salted boiling water until just al dente. Reserve about 1 cup pasta water before draining.
- Cut guanciale into small pieces and fry over medium heat until crisp and the fat renders. Remove from heat.
- Whisk eggs with the grated Pecorino and a generous amount of black pepper.
- Add hot, drained pasta to the pan with guanciale and its fat. Remove the pan from direct heat, then quickly pour in the egg-cheese mixture and toss vigorously, adding reserved pasta water a little at a time until you get a creamy sauce (no scrambling). Adjust with more cheese or water as needed. Serve immediately with extra Pecorino and pepper.

2) Fettuccine Alfredo (traditional style)
Ingredients (serves 2–3):
- 250 g fettuccine
- 100 g unsalted butter
- 100 g finely grated Parmigiano-Reggiano
- Salt (for the pasta water)
- Freshly ground black pepper

Method:
- Cook fettuccine in well-salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve some pasta water before draining.
- In a warm pan, melt the butter (you can add a splash of cream if you prefer a richer, saucier version).
- Add the drained pasta to the pan, remove from heat, and sprinkle in the grated Parmigiano. Toss quickly, adding reserved pasta water as needed to create a silky emulsion that clings to the noodles. Serve with extra cheese and pepper.

If you’d like, I can send printable recipe cards, exact measurements scaled for a different number of servings, or photos from the class. Want me to save these as a draft first or make any edits?

Cheers,

args.subject: Baking tips from Chef Pierre — laminating dough & macaronage
args.body:
Hi Alice,

I wanted to share some fantastic baking tips Chef Pierre taught during our pastry class:

• Laminating dough (for croissants/puff pastry): keep the butter cold and work quickly; use the roll-and-fold technique with several "turns" and chill the dough between turns; chill the dough well before shaping and baking to maintain distinct layers for flakiness.

• Macaronage (for macarons): fold the batter until it flows like thick lava and holds a glossy sheen — don’t overmix; tap the baking sheet to release air bubbles; let piped macarons rest until a skin forms before baking for smooth tops and proper feet.

He also emphasized accuracy (use a kitchen scale), sifting dry ingredients, and controlling ingredient temperatures (butter and eggs) for the best results.

If you’d like, I can send full recipes, photos from the class, or a step-by-step checklist for practicing these techniques.

Best,
[Your Name]
